Empirical Research Plan: “Finance and Growth Across Countries, 1960-1995”

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Chosen method: Instrumental-Variables (2SLS) estimation in a panel framework (country- and year-fixed effects).

Rationale
•  Endogeneity: Financial depth (Private Credit/GDP) is jointly determined with growth (reverse causality) and is correlated with unobserved institutions.  
•  Large-N, small-T: 129 countries × 36 years provides enough cross-section and time variation for consistent IV with fixed effects.  
•  Plausible external instruments exist: legal-origin–based variables and other deeply historical factors that shaped financial systems centuries before 1960 but are plausibly unrelated to post-1960 growth except through finance.

Core specification  
    Δln GDPpc_it = β · Finance_it + γ X_it + μ_i + τ_t + ε_it  
with Finance_it = Private Credit/GDP and X_it baseline controls; instrument Finance_it with Z_it described below.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable
• Finance_it = private domestic credit extended by deposit-taking institutions to the private sector, divided by GDP (continuous).

Instruments (Z_it)  
1.  Legal-origin dummies: English, French, German, Scandinavian.  
2.  Interactions of those dummies with a global time trend (t) → allows year-varying exogenous shifts.  
3.  Pre-1913 bank-branch density (or 1913 Private Credit/GDP from Rousseau & Sylla) – time-invariant but strongly correlated with modern depth.

These instruments are combined so that there is within-country variation (coming from the interacted terms) and strong cross-sectional power (from historical levels).

Control group / counterfactual
• Countries whose predicted financial depth from the instruments is low serve as the counterfactual for those whose predicted depth is high.  
• Because treatment is continuous, the counterfactual is embedded in the 2SLS regression rather than an explicit DID grouping.

Timing
• Annual panel 1960-1995. Finance_it is measured at t-1 (lagged 1 year) to reduce mechanical simultaneity.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Relevance: Legal origin and pre-1913 finance strongly predict post-1960 Private Credit/GDP (first-stage F > 10).  
  Plausibility: Documented in La Porta et al. (1998) and historians’ evidence.

A2. Exclusion Restriction: Conditional on standard growth covariates, legal origin affects post-1960 growth only via today’s financial development, not via other channels.  
  Discussion: Could be violated because legal origin shapes broader institutions; we mitigate via rich controls (rule-of-law, democracy, trade openness) and country fixed effects.

A3. Monotonicity: Countries with a given legal origin do not experience decreases in Finance_it when the instrument predicts an increase (“no defiers”).  
  Plausible because the channels (creditor protection, contract enforceability) work in one direction.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): A country’s growth responds only to its own financial development, not other countries’ (no strong spillovers).  
  More plausible given national capital controls for much of the period, but we will test for global spillovers via spatial lags.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats & Mitigations
────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Omitted institutional factors correlated with legal origin.  
 • Add broad institutional controls (Polity IV democracy index, Fraser Econ-Freedom legal system & property-rights sub-index).  
 • Include country FE (μ_i) to absorb time-invariant culture/legal factors.  
 • Use over-ID tests (Hansen J) to detect mis-specification.

T2. Weak instruments once FE added.  
 • Report first-stage F-statistics of the interacted instruments (>10 is target).  
 • Collapse the panel to 5-year averages to strengthen signal if yearly noise is large.  
 • Alternative historical instrument (1913 PC/GDP) to show robustness.

T3. Measurement error in Private Credit/GDP.  
 • Use multiple finance measures (Liquid Liabilities/GDP, Stock-Market Capitalization/GDP).  
 • Errors-in-vars bias is alleviated by IV (relying on Z, not noisy Finance).

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
#====================#
# 0.  Libraries      #
#====================#
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)      # fast FE and IV
library(modelsummary)

#====================#
# 1.  Load data      #
#====================#
panel <- read_csv("finance_growth_1960_1995.csv")

#====================#
# 2.  Variable prep  #
#====================#
panel <- panel %>%
  mutate(year          = as.integer(year),
         ln_GDPpc      = log(GDP_per_capita_const),
         g_GDPpc       = 100*(ln_GDPpc - lag(ln_GDPpc)), # % growth
         finance       = Private_Credit_GDP,
         L.finance     = lag(finance),                   # 1-yr lag
         # legal-origin dummies
         english       = if_else(legal_origin=="English",1,0),
         french        = if_else(legal_origin=="French",1,0),
         german        = if_else(legal_origin=="German",1,0),
         scandinavian  = if_else(legal_origin=="Scandinavian",1,0),
         # interacted instruments
         eng_trend     = english*year,
         fre_trend     = french*year,
         ger_trend     = german*year,
         sca_trend     = scandinavian*year)

#====================#
# 3.  Main 2SLS      #
#====================#
iv_formula <- 
  g_GDPpc ~ L.finance + ln_GDPpc + human_capital + trade_open + pop_growth | 
            eng_trend + fre_trend + ger_trend + sca_trend + 
            ln_GDPpc + human_capital + trade_open + pop_growth

iv_main <- feols(iv_formula,
                 data = panel,
                 cluster = ~country + year, # two-way clustering
                 fixef  = ~country + year)

summary(iv_main, stage = 1)   # show 1st-stage & 2nd-stage

#====================#
# 4.  Robustness     #
#====================#
# (i) Alternative finance measure
iv_alt <- feols(
  g_GDPpc ~ lag(Liquid_Liabilities_GDP) + ln_GDPpc + human_capital | 
            eng_trend + fre_trend + ger_trend + sca_trend + 
            ln_GDPpc + human_capital,
  data = panel, fixef = ~country + year, cluster = ~country+year)

# (ii) 5-year averages
panel5 <- panel %>% 
          filter(year %% 5 == 0)

iv_5yr <- feols(iv_formula, data = panel5,
                fixef=~country+year, cluster=~country)

# Present results
modelsummary(list(Main = iv_main, AltFin = iv_alt, `5-yr` = iv_5yr),
             statistic = "({std.error}) [{p.value}]",
             output = "markdown")
```

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────
Theory (Schumpeterian/AK models and empirical consensus) predicts a positive link.  
Priors: A 10 percentage-point increase in Private Credit/GDP (≈0.3 SD) raises annual GDP-per-capita growth by 0.15–0.25 ppt. Thus β ≈ 0.015–0.025.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist (IV) – Self-Assessment
────────────────────────────────────────
C1 Relevance (1) – historical/legal instruments strongly predict finance.  
C2 Exclusion Restriction (0) – plausible but contestable; cannot fully rule out other institution channels.  
C3 Monotonicity (1) – no known cases where stronger creditor rights reduced credit.  
C4 Common Support (1) – wide variation in predicted and actual finance across all income levels.  
C5 Robust Inference (1) – two-way clustering, over-ID tests, and multiple instruments planned.

Total: 4 / 5.
